scope: Raw Wi-Fi PHY bytes; RX correctness before performance and TX

rfc_discovery.note: RFC discovery yielded no PHY authority. IEEE publications supply the evidence below.

reviewed_clauses: 36.3.11.7 U-SIG content, CRC, encoding and modulation

facts.anchor: L-SIG and RL-SIG draft text; later CC36 resolution 11-21/1101r1
facts.fact: An EHT PPDU uses a 6 Mb/s L-SIG whose LENGTH is divisible by three, followed by an RL-SIG that repeats L-SIG. This combination separates EHT from non-HT, HT, VHT and HE before the two BPSK U-SIG symbols are interpreted. A 20 MHz observation can recover duplicated pre-EHT signaling even when U-SIG declares a wider PPDU, but that does not make the uncaptured wider DATA recoverable.

facts.anchor: 36.3.11.7 Tables36-19/21; CRC computation; encoding and modulation; later LB275 resolution 11-23/1425r1
facts.fact: EHT U-SIG carries two 26-bit parts, encoded continuously with rate-half BCC and the 52-tone interleaver. Its CRC protects the first 42 information bits and is followed by six zero tail bits. PHY version zero identifies EHT. UL/DL together with the two-bit PPDU type distinguishes EHT MU OFDMA, single-user, non-OFDMA MU-MIMO and EHT TB interpretations. For EHT MU, the version-dependent fields also carry puncturing information, EHT-SIG MCS and EHT-SIG symbol count; for EHT TB they carry two spatial-reuse values. The current parser checks integrity and Validate states but does not itself admit or decode EHT DATA. Published-standard clause review remains required before final qualification.

The first 52-bit EHT-SIG encoding block for non-OFDMA signaling contains 20 common bits, the first 22-bit user field, a four-bit CRC over the preceding 42 bits, and six zero tail bits. The common portion carries spatial reuse, EHT-LTF size and guard interval, EHT-LTF count, LDPC-extra-symbol, pre-FEC padding, packet-extension disambiguity, Disregard bits, and number of users. The published D5 example's protected bits independently produce CRC 1110. A single-user field carries STA-ID, MCS, NSS, beamforming, coding, and a preserved reserved/disregard bit. For non-OFDMA MU-MIMO, the first and remaining fields instead carry STA-ID, MCS, coding, and a raw spatial-configuration index; remaining users are grouped into independently protected one- or two-user blocks. The bit and IQ receivers cover complete chains of two through eight MU-MIMO users and reset BCC for every independently terminated block. OFDMA and EHT DATA remain separate work. Published-standard clause review remains required before final qualification.

facts.anchor: 36.3.12.8.6; related waveform equation and content-channel text in 11-21/0140r2
facts.fact: EHT-SIG MCS values 0, 1, 3 and 15 all use rate-one-half BCC. MCS15 is MCS0 with DCM. EHT-SIG uses the same BCC interleaver parameters as HE-SIG-A/HE-SIG-B, 52 data tones per 4 microsecond OFDM symbol, an 0.8 microsecond guard interval, and pilot sequence position n+4. Its upper-half PAPR rotation follows the HE-SIG-B rule except that MCS15 uses unity PAPR rotation. For a 52-bit single-user encoding block in 20 MHz, the resulting EHT-SIG lengths are two, one, one and four symbols for MCS0, MCS1, MCS3 and MCS15 respectively.

VHT SU STBC maps one DATA stream to two space-time streams using the same conjugate-pair operation as HT. Two VHT-LTF data columns use the first two HT P-matrix columns, but every training pilot row repeats P's first row. Thus the two training pilot observations are the combined channel and its negative. SIG-B DATA uses the first P column, and its pilots are common across streams; for two streams both observe the combined channel. VHT20 DATA pilots use the single-stream rotating pattern regardless of STBC, unlike HT's two-stream pilot patterns. With two transmit chains, pre-VHT cyclic shifts are 0/-200 ns and VHT shifts are 0/-400 ns.

VHT LDPC receive length is the whole-octet capacity after removing the 16 SERVICE bits from initial-symbol-count times NDBPS; unlike BCC it removes no tail bits. The LDPC extra flag accounts for one extra symbol without STBC or two with STBC, consistently with the forward coding procedure. A decoded SIG-B must be checked against the CRC carried in descrambled SERVICE; final incomplete octets are discarded as padding.

VHT SU LDPC reuses HT codeword selection and rate matching, but its encoded information includes scrambled SERVICE, PSDU and PHY padding. Npld is initial symbol count times NDBPS; initial symbols round (8*APEP_LENGTH+16) up to an STBC symbol group, and initial available coded bits are that count times NCBPS. SIG-A's extra-symbol bit records whether the puncturing rule adds a symbol group. For VHT20, LDPC tone mapping permutes whole constellation symbols with distance 4: input tone index k goes to 4*(k mod 13)+floor(k/13). BCC does not use this mapping.

facts.anchor: VHT field 21 known/flags, bandwidth and mcs_nss tables; A-MPDU field 20 EOF flags
facts.fact: VHT metadata is 12 bytes aligned to two bytes. GI and bandwidth validity use known bits 0x0004 and 0x0040; STBC, disambiguation, LDPC extra symbol, beamforming, group ID and partial AID have distinct validity bits. Radiotap bandwidth value 0 denotes 20 MHz; these codes are not SIG-A bandwidth codes. Each user byte has NSS in its low nibble and MCS in its high nibble; NSS zero invalidates that user's MCS/coding and MCS 15 means unknown. A present user's coding bit is meaningful without a separate known bit. NSS differs from NSTS when STBC is used. Group 0/63 means SU when group is known. A-MPDU EOF is meaningful only with flag 0x0080; its value is flag 0x0040.

VHT delimiter B2..3 carry the high two length bits and B4..15 the low twelve; B0 is EOF and B1 reserved. EOF=1/nonzero length marks an S-MPDU, which must be the only nonzero-length subframe. EOF=1/zero length marks padding and cannot precede an S-MPDU. No EOF=0 subframe may follow EOF=1. Final alignment padding and zero to three trailing EOF octets have unspecified contents. The HT 65535-octet total limit does not apply to VHT; its 1048575-octet limit is pre-EOF.

VHT-SIG-A uses BPSK then QBPSK data tones with unrotated pilots p1,p2. VHT-STF20 equals HT-STF20 and VHT-LTF20 equals HT-LTF20. VHT-SIG-B uses p3/P0; DATA uses p[n+4]/P[n]. Tone scaling uses 52 for L-LTF/L-SIG/SIG-A and 56 for VHT-LTF/SIG-B/DATA. A single nonzero-length delimiter may carry EOF=1 (S-MPDU); final subframe padding, EOF padding delimiters and trailing octets fill PSDU capacity under 10.12.6. RX symbol and PSDU length equations confirm the previously reviewed timing and BCC layout.

For VHT BCC with one encoder, DATA consists of 16 SERVICE bits, PSDU, zero through seven PHY pad bits, then six zero tail bits. SERVICE/PSDU/pad are scrambled with a nonzero seed; tail is not scrambled. PSDU length is floor((NSYM*NDBPS-22)/8). SERVICE bits 0-7 are zero and bits 8-15 carry the SIG-B CRC, c7 first. The final BCC trellis state is zero, unlike the existing HT layout with scrambled padding after its tail.

For 20 MHz and one spatial stream, MCS 0-7 have 52 data tones and the same per-symbol coding/modulation dimensions as HT MCS 0-7. MCS 8 uses 256-QAM, rate 3/4, 416 coded bits and 312 data bits per symbol, with one BCC encoder. MCS 9 is explicitly not valid for this bandwidth and spatial-stream count.

Visually reviewed all four quadrants. Each axis uses levels -15,-13,-11,-9,-7,-5,-3,-1,1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15 with first-transmitted-bit-first labels 0000,0001,0011,0010,0110,0111,0101,0100,1100,1101,1111,1110,1010,1011,1001,1000. The first four bits label I and the next four Q. Complex constellation normalization is 1/sqrt(170).

VHT uses 6 Mb/s L-SIG, whose length is three times the four-microsecond duration units after the initial 20 microseconds, minus three. VHT-LTF counts for 1..8 space-time streams are 1,2,4,4,6,6,8,8. DATA begins at 36+4*NLTF microseconds. Short-GI DATA has 3.6-microsecond symbols but its signaled duration rounds up to four-microsecond units. SIG-A disambiguation is one exactly when short GI is used and NSYM mod 10 equals 9. DATA symbol end and signaled duration can differ. STBC requires even symbol groups.

VHT20 SIG-B has 20 field bits and six zero tail bits. SU uses 17 length bits and three reserved ones; MU uses 16 length bits and four MCS bits. Length is ceil(APEP_LENGTH/4). VHT NDP is SU, has no DATA, and uses the fixed pre-tail pattern 00000111010001000010. In MU that same pattern is ordinary length/MCS data. SIG-B's CRC covers its first 20 bits and is transmitted c7 first in descrambled SERVICE bits 8..15; SERVICE bits 0..7 are zero. The 20 MHz one-stream BPSK interleaver uses 13 columns and four rows. SIG-B parsing alone cannot assert CRC integrity.

VHT-SIG-A consists of two 24-bit parts, BCC encoded together at rate one-half and interleaved per 48-tone symbol. The first symbol's data tones use BPSK and the second QBPSK. Group IDs 0 and 63 select SU field interpretation; other IDs select four MU user positions. CRC covers the first 34 bits using the HT polynomial, followed by six zero tail bits. Bandwidth code 3 does not distinguish contiguous 160 MHz from 80+80 MHz. Header integrity alone does not admit the DATA configuration.

HT-ELTFs sound spatial dimensions not used by DATA. Data HT-LTFs excite Q columns 1 through NSTS; extension HT-LTFs excite the following NESS columns with their own P rows and columns, cyclic shifts indexed within NESS, and normalization by sqrt(NESS). NESS1/2/3 adds 1/2/4 four-microsecond fields after data training, before DATA. NSS1/STBC0 allows NESS0..3, while NSS1/STBC1 allows NESS0..2. The original DATA channel estimates remain applicable after these extension fields. Sounding PPDUs set Not Sounding to zero.

For two transmit chains, the non-HT portion of mixed format uses cyclic shifts 0 and -200 ns, including HT-SIG. Two space-time streams use cyclic shifts 0 and -400 ns in the HT portion and DATA; greenfield uses these HT shifts throughout. NSTS2 requires two data HT-LTFs. With no extension streams, mixed DATA begins at 40 us and greenfield DATA at 28 us. Additional extension training counts are 0/1/2/4 for NESS0/1/2/3; NSTS+NESS must not exceed four and total HT-LTF count must not exceed five.

NSS=1 with MCS0-7 and STBC=1 uses two space-time streams. For consecutive constellation symbols (a,b), stream 1 transmits (a,b) and stream 2 transmits (-conj(b),conj(a)). The first two HT-LTF columns are (1,1) and (-1,1). Two-STS pilot patterns are [1,1,-1,-1] and [1,-1,-1,1], cyclically rotated across symbols before polarity multiplication. The two-data-symbol inverse requires both effective channels, not the single-stream equalizer.

HT-greenfield omits legacy SIGNAL and uses HT-GF-STF, HT-LTF1 and HT-SIG before any remaining HT-LTFs and DATA. With one space-time stream and no extension streams these first three fields each last 8 us and DATA begins at 24 us. HT-LTF1 has a 1.6 us cyclic prefix and two 3.2 us long symbols. HT-SIG contents match mixed format. DATA pilot polarity uses offset z=2, not mixed-format z=3. The short-GI note excludes greenfield with one spatial stream and DATA immediately following HT-SIG.

MCS metadata separately qualifies bandwidth, index, GI, format, coding, STBC and extension-stream information. Unknown fields are not zero-valued observations. A-MPDU status identifies aggregation with a capture-device reference number; that identifier is channel-scoped and is not an IQ delimiter offset.

HT A-MPDU length is at most 65535 octets. Delimiters are four octets with signature 0x4e; HT uses the 12-bit low MPDU length subfield. Nonfinal subframes align to four octets with unspecified padding; the final HT subframe is unpadded. Length-zero delimiters contain no MPDU. CRC protects the preceding 16 transmitted bits using the HT CRC polynomial and all-one initial state; C7 is transmitted as B16. Annex O.2 describes four-byte resynchronization and permits other receiver algorithms.

Systematic LDPC codewords satisfy H*c^T=0. Block lengths 648/1296/1944 support rates 1/2, 2/3, 3/4 and 5/6. Subblocks are zero matrices or identity matrices cyclically shifted right; sizes are 27/54/81 respectively. All twelve prototypes have been reviewed.

LDPC uses PSDU plus 16 SERVICE bits without BCC tail. Codeword sizing, shortening, puncturing and repetition depend on available coded symbol bits. Excess puncturing can add one symbol group. Shortening and puncturing remove trailing information and parity bits, respectively; repetition copies the shortened codeword from its beginning. LDPC bypasses the BCC frequency interleaver.
One-stream MCS 0-7 uses 52 data carriers and 26/52/78/104/156/208/234/260 data bits per symbol. BCC DATA contains 16 SERVICE bits, PSDU, six tail bits and padding. Rate 5/6 retains A0 B0 A1 B2 A3 B4.

HT20 training extends L-LTF with +1 on the two extra negative tones and -1 on the two extra positive tones. BCC interleaving uses 13 columns. One-stream pilots rotate [1,1,1,-1] across DATA symbols; mixed-format polarity starts at p3.
HT-mixed uses an L_DATARATE of 6 Mb/s. L-SIG length describes protection duration, not the HT PSDU byte count.
HT-SIG comprises two 24-bit parts. Data tones use BPSK rotated 90 degrees; pilots are not rotated.
CRC protects the first 34 HT-SIG bits, with polynomial x^8+x^2+x+1, all-one initialization and complemented output, C7 first.
HT-STF duration is 4 microseconds; its 20 MHz frequency sequence is identical to L-STF.

242RU nonDCM BCC interleaving uses26 columns and9*NBPSCS rows with VHT permutations. BPSK through256QAM reuse VHT constellation mapping. Pilot tones are -116,-90,-48,-22,22,48,90,116; pilot values rotate [1,1,1,-1,-1,1,1,1] by DATA symbol index. SU DATA uses legacy polarity index n+4. One-stream/one-RU waveform normalization is1/sqrt242. Packet extension has arbitrary content but DATA average power. This kernel does not yet publish MAC frames.

HE BCC uses one encoder. SERVICE and PSDU plus pre-FEC PHY padding are scrambled; six zero tail bits follow that padding and terminate the encoder. Puncturing uses the legacy1/2,2/3,3/4 patterns and HT5/6 pattern. Post-FEC padding follows meaningful coded bits in each last STBC-group symbol. DCM BPSK/NSS1 inserts one arbitrary filler after2*NDBPS coded bits:50 for106RU or116 for242RU. ER context must be established before using the shared bandwidth field as an RU selector. SERVICE is16 zero bits before scrambling with a nonzero seed. These facts do not establish IQ or MAC/FCS qualification.

HE20 SU uses234 data tones, or117 with DCM. DCM supports MCS0/1/3/4 with1/2 spatial streams and noSTBC. BCC is limited to MCS0-9 and<=4 spatial streams; MCS10/11 requireLDPC. Short padding segments use60 or30 data tones. PSDU length floors the data budget minus16SERVICE bits and6BCC tail bits to octets; LDPC has no tail. LDPC extra-segment signaling advances padding factor or wraps4to1 while adding one STBC symbol group; receiver reverses that adjustment for the payload budget. DCM BPSK/NSS1 uses58 data bits per symbol and BCC inserts one arbitrary filler after116 coded bits.

SU uses m=2 in L-SIG duration. HE preamble in receiver duration inversion excludes legacy20us and includes RL-SIG, SIG-A, STF and LTF symbols. Receiver symbol count floors the duration quotient then subtracts PE disambiguity; PE duration floors the remaining duration to4us increments. Midambles repeat the initial HE-LTF field every10 or20 DATA symbols with NSTS<=4, but are omitted before a sole final DATA symbol or after the last symbol. STBC is restricted to one spatial stream/two space-time streams without DCM. This timing implementation does not establish DATA decoding or MIMO reception.

ER supports one DATA stream, MCS0-2 on242 tones and only MCS0 on upper106. The106 allocation has102 DATA tones, halved to51 for DCM; its short segments use24 or12 DATA tones. BPSK/DCM data bits per full symbol floor to25 for106 or58 for242. With BCC a filler follows2*NDBPS coded bits. Format-aware capacity arithmetic preserves SU bandwidth semantics, reverses LDPC extra-segment signaling for PSDU length, and checks STBC grouping. Independent forward padding fixtures do not establish upper106 IQ recovery.

ER STF/LTF amplitudes are boosted by sqrt2 relative to DATA; the receiver divides trained channel estimates by sqrt2. Midambles repeat the initial LTF and require the same correction. DATA pilot polarity uses n+2+N_HE-SIG-A+N_HE-SIG-B, hence n+6 for ER's four-symbol SIG-A with no SIG-B. The242-tone DATA mapping, BCC/LDPC, DCM and STBC kernels share SU geometry after ER timing and scaling are restored. Independent complete waveforms validate raw bytes and aggregate FCS offline, not RF interoperability.

ER SU uses m=1 in L-SIG duration and four SIG-A symbols (16us), adding160 samples at20Msps relative to SU. Duration inversion uses (L_LENGTH+4)/3 legacy symbols, with a preamble160 samples longer. ER supports one DATA stream, optionally mapped to two space-time streams with STBC. Its242-tone and upper106-tone allocations share the DATA symbol clock and preamble duration. Independent forward timelines check DATA, midamble and PE offsets; this primitive does not establish ER payload recovery.

facts.anchor: Table 27-31; Equations 27-5/40/41/42/58; Table 27-12; printed536 visually checked
facts.fact: HE20 SU 1x training uses 60 active tones at multiples of four and a 64-sample useful period with 800ns GI. 2x uses 122 even tones and a 128-sample useful period with 800ns or 1600ns GI. Both sequences span signed indices -122 through 122. Equation27-5 defines the HE-LTF normalization denominator as RU size divided by4 or2, without rounding:60.5 and121 for a242-tone RU, not populated-tone counts60 and122. Receiver inference: short-FFT channel gain converts to256-point DATA gain by sqrt(256/NFFT). Regularized finite-delay least-squares fitting is an implementation estimator, not a standard-mandated exact channel reconstruction. It models four precursor samples and delays inside the guard interval; arbitrary channels outside that model are not guaranteed.

HE SU STF lasts80 samples at20Msps, using14 nonzero tones at spacing16 with the M sequence times(1+j)/sqrt2 and zero DC. One-stream one-RU normalization is1/sqrt14. The4x HE-LTF sequence has242 nonzero tones at signedindices-122..-2 and2..122; normalization is1/sqrt242. P and R first-row/first-column factors are1 for one stream. 4x training supports800ns or3200ns GI via the SU signaling interpretation; HE fields may have different spatial mapping from pre-HE fields when Beam Change is set.

The HE DATA DFT period is12.8us with78.125kHz spacing. HE-LTF1x/2x/4x useful durations are3.2/6.4/12.8us. At20Msps these correspond to64/128/256 samples; GI samples are separate. Private natural-order unnormalized forward transforms support subsequent channel estimation and DATA demapping without changing legacy64-point processing.

HE BCC uses one encoder, at most four spatial streams and MCS0-9, with RU sizes at most242 tones. MCS10/11 and larger RUs require LDPC. Header interpretation does not substitute for these DATA admission checks. The IQ prefix corpus selects LDPC for MCS10/11.

HE L-SIG and RL-SIG repeat the same header with valid parity and 6Mb/s rate; LENGTH remainder1 selects SU/TB, with HE-SIG-A Format1 selecting SU. SU HE-SIG-A has two real-axis BPSK symbols. L-SIG edge tones -28,-27,27,28 carry -1,-1,-1,1, repeated in RL-SIG. L-LTF normalization uses52 tones and an additional epsilon=sqrt(52/56), making its per-tone amplitude match 56-tone signaling; L-STF also has that epsilon. Pilot polarities use indices0,1,2,3 for these four signaling symbols. These checks do not establish DATA integrity or admit every signaled mode.

HE SU signaling contains 26+26 bits, with 42 CRC-protected bits, four CRC bits and six zero tail bits. Reserved bits A1.B14 and A2.B14 are one; BCC requires A2.B8 one. Doppler changes NSTS and midamble interpretation. DCM=STBC=1 with GI/LTF code3 means neither applied and 4x LTF with 0.8us GI; other codes in that combination are reserved. Signaling BPSK interleaving uses 13 columns and 4 rows, with continuous rate-half BCC over both symbols. Format context must distinguish SU from MU, TB and ER SU before interpreting these fields.

HE encodes scrambled SERVICE, PSDU and pre-FEC padding without BCC tail bits. Initial available coded positions use the last padding segment, not complete OFDM symbols. The inherited puncturing thresholds select an extra segment: initial factor3 adds the remaining full-symbol portion; other factors add one short segment per STBC-group symbol. Factor4 wraps to1 and adds a symbol group. Codeword count/size and shortening precede this adjustment; puncturing is recomputed afterward. Post-FEC padding is excluded from LDPC observations. Rate-matching geometry and codeword tests do not establish HE LDPC IQ reception.

HE 1024-QAM uses five label bits per axis and normalization 1/sqrt(682). For a non-DCM 242-tone RU, LDPC tone mapping has NSD=234 and DTM=9: transmitted data-tone index t(k)=9*(k mod26)+floor(k/26). Indices exclude pilots. Independent constellation and transpose fixtures qualify private demapping primitives, not complete LDPC IQ reception, DCM or spatial-stream separation.

Midambles repeat the preamble HE-LTF fields after groups of10 or20 DATA symbols, excluding after the last symbol and before a sole last symbol. DATA scrambling and encoding do not change. Doppler may be set even when a short PPDU contains no midamble. The receiver reuses the LTF estimator at the independently derived offsets, keeps DATA pilot indices and absolute CFO phase, and resets the residual phase-slope estimate after each refresh. Piecewise FIR-channel fixtures qualify this estimator behavior, not arbitrary Doppler tracking.

HE242 DCM pairs117 lower DATA tones with117 upper tones. BPSK upper symbols use sign(-1)^(k+117); QPSK uses conjugation; 16-QAM exchanges adjacent label bits. LDPC permutes each half separately with DTM_DCM=9 before transmission. BCC instead uses13 interleaver columns and9*NBPSCS rows, and BPSK one-stream BCC inserts a filler after116 coded bits. The receiver combines joint label distances weighted by channel power. Supported MCSs are0/1/3/4; DCM cannot be combined with STBC. Table27-79 specifies58 data bits for one-stream DCM BPSK.

HE shares the split 14-bit MPDU delimiter length with VHT. For nonzero length, EOF/Tag can mark a tagged MPDU within an acknowledgment-enabled aggregate, not necessarily the final frame. Only a zero-length tagged delimiter starts EOF padding; it must not precede a later nonempty MPDU. The raw-byte scanner preserves tags without asserting acknowledgment-context validity, retains FCS, and emits only integrity-valid frames. PHY capacity and caller storage bounds remain separate admission requirements.
HE-SIG-A CRC covers 42 bits. The underlying eight-bit polynomial is inherited from HT, but only four complemented output bits are transmitted, C7 first.

ER SU uses L-SIG length modulo three equal to two, and A1/A1-R/A2/A2-R signaling. Only A1-R DATA tones are QBPSK. Original halves are interleaved; repeated halves bypass interleaving. Pilots retain the polarity sequence. L-STF/L-LTF have a sqrt(2) boost, L-SIG/RL-SIG boost only their four added edge tones, and SIG-A has no such boost. ER permits one spatial stream, MCS0-2 on242 or MCS0 on upper106 within20MHz; STBC may use two space-time streams. Signaling integrity does not qualify DATA.

HE STBC maps one DATA stream to two space-time streams and excludes DCM. DATA uses the VHT conjugate/sign pair mapping. SU HE-LTF uses P on DATA tones but R (the repeated first P row) on pilots, so pilots do not independently identify the two channels. DATA pilots are copied to both STS before cyclic shifts. Two STS use two training symbols and the second stream has a -400 ns cyclic shift.
